interpretation.read_as: For this step (WP-01's step 5, the last one, 'CI lint and type checking'): add ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy on src/sulis_workflows/definition/ to .github/workflows/ci.yml, and make the code actually pass all three — this is also WP-01's own overall acceptance criterion A6 ('pytest, ruff and mypy pass on Python 3.10-3.12 in CI'), so this step is what finally proves it.

decisions.headline: Invoke ruff and mypy as `python -m ruff`/`python -m mypy` in CI, not the bare `ruff`/`mypy` commands.
decisions.problem: This development container has two separate installations of both ruff and mypy on PATH — an older, differently-configured one (from an earlier ad-hoc `pip install ruff mypy` before this PR added them to pyproject.toml's dev extra) and the one `pip install -e ".[dev]"` actually installs into this project's environment. The bare commands resolved to the wrong (stale, unrelated) installation and gave misleadingly clean or inconsistent results; `python -m ruff`/`python -m mypy` always resolve against the same interpreter/environment `pip install -e ".[dev]"` populated, which is what CI's own `pip install -e ".[dev]"` step guarantees too.
options_rejected: Trust the bare `ruff`/`mypy` commands, since real GitHub Actions runners start from a clean environment with only one installation: rejected — cheap to make robust regardless, and a contributor's own machine (not just this container) can have the exact same kind of PATH ambiguity from an unrelated global install; the fix costs nothing and removes a whole class of 'works here, not there' report.

evidence.claim: Bare `mypy` reported false pydantic import errors from files outside this PR's scope and missed a real error `python -m mypy` caught (validate.py:416); bare `ruff check` reported zero findings while `python -m ruff check` (the pip-installed 0.16.8, matching pyproject.toml's dev extra) found 33, all legitimate.
evidence.source: measured directly while running both forms side by side in this session

decisions.revisit_if: Never expected — this is a robustness fix, not a project-specific one.

measured.subject: ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy, and pytest together on src/sulis_workflows/definition/ (+tests/definition/ for ruff)
measured.method: Ran all four via python -m, using the exact same dev-extra install CI will use.
measured.result: All four clean: 0 ruff findings, 0 reformatting needed, 0 mypy errors, 200/200 tests passing.

measured.subject: The same four checks on Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12
measured.method: Ran pytest in isolated 3.10/3.12 venvs (as in every prior step); ruff/mypy are version-format/type checks rather than runtime-dependent, and target-version=py310/python_version=3.10 in pyproject.toml is what makes them honest about the oldest supported interpreter, rather than re-running the type checker under each interpreter binary.

lessons.maxim: Before trusting a linter's or type checker's "all clean" result in an unfamiliar environment, confirm the binary on PATH is actually the one the project's own dependency manifest installs — a stale or unrelated global install can silently under-report (or over-report) findings with no visible error.
lessons.incident: A prior ad-hoc `pip install ruff mypy` (before this PR added them to pyproject.toml's dev extra) had put a different, older ruff and a differently-linked mypy on PATH; the bare commands gave a false-clean ruff result and a false-error-laden mypy result, both wrong in ways that would have been easy to trust and move on from.
lessons.destination: any future PR in this repository that adds or runs a lint/type-check tool for the first time in a session
